title: Extract one step-derived slider readout-precision helper for the materials sliders
body:
## Summary
The step-derived readout rule now exists as two private copies (configurator ParametersSection and style-transfer AdjustSlider) plus a scale rule in PropertyBar.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialParameterConfigurator/ParametersSection.tsx:17 and src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/AdjustSlider.tsx:7 each define `readoutDecimals(step)` identically (this round added the second copy because the first is outside this context and unexported). src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/PropertyBar.tsx carries a third, scale-based rule. A fourth slider will hand-roll a fifth. Fixed = one exported helper (e.g. in @/lib/format) consumed by all three, with the existing precision tests pinning it.

## Flow
- add `readoutDecimals(step)` to @/lib/format with a unit test
- import it in ParametersSection and AdjustSlider, delete both private copies
- run ParametersSection.precision + AdjustSlider.precision + PropertyBar.precision

## Expected impact
Developers: one place for the precision rule; a future change cannot fix one slider and not its pair (the exact drift fixed twice this week). Could break: nothing if the three precision suites stay green.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the readout precision rule
Before: 2 identical private readoutDecimals copies + 1 sibling rule (grep `function readoutDecimals` under src/components/modules/content/materials = 2)
After: predicted 1 exported helper, 0 private copies
Method: simulation - ParametersSection.tsx is in material-configurator, outside this round's paths (veto 1), so the probe could not be applied here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of `function readoutDecimals` under src/components/modules/content/materials (2 -> 0) with the three *.precision tests green

title: Guard the style-transfer FileReader so an older pick cannot overwrite a newer one
body:
## Summary
acceptFile starts a FileReader per pick with no latest-wins token; an older, larger read finishing last replaces the newer reference image.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/useMaterialStyleTransfer.ts acceptFile: each call creates a reader whose onload unconditionally sets imageDataUrl and resets the analysis. Two picks in quick succession (a 9 MB PNG then a 200 KB JPG) can complete out of order, leaving the first file shown while the user believes the second is loaded. The analyze path got a latest-wins token this round (03a77b0f); the read path is its unguarded pair. Fixed = a read token minted per acceptFile, compared in onload/onerror (registry client-state/async-race-guards).

## Flow
- user picks big.png, then immediately small.jpg
- small.jpg onload sets imageDataUrl
- big.png onload lands later and overwrites it -> panel shows the file the user replaced

## Expected impact
Designers swapping references quickly see the right image; could break: nothing beyond the hook, the stale suite covers the analyze half.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a superseded file read is inert
Before: 0 of 2 read completions guarded (onload, onerror)
After: predicted 2 of 2 guarded; the newer pick always wins
Method: simulation - needs a controllable FileReader stub (jsdom reads complete on its own schedule); not built this round for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/useMaterialStyleTransfer.ts acceptFile: `reader.onload = () => { ... setImageDataUrl(reader.result as string) ... }` - no token compare
instrument: vi.stubGlobal FileReader with manually fired onload; pick A then B, fire B then A, assert imageDataUrl === B

title: Collapse the four parallel style-transfer override states into one overrides record
body:
## Summary
The hook keeps roughness/metallic/emissive/surface overrides as four useState pairs, resets them by a hand-kept list in two places, and drills 8 of AnalysisResults' 16 props for them.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/useMaterialStyleTransfer.ts holds 4 override states; acceptFile and handleClearImage each call the 4 setters (8 hand-listed resets) and handleGenerate rebuilds `adjustments` from them. index.tsx destructures 26 hook fields and passes 16 props to AnalysisResults.tsx. Adding a fifth override (subsurface is already displayed) means editing 6 sites; forgetting one reset leaks an override onto the next image. Fixed = `overrides: Partial<Pick<AnalyzedProperties, ...>>` with `setOverride(key, v)` / `clearOverrides()`, AnalysisResults taking `overrides` + `setOverride`.

## Flow
- introduce overrides record + setOverride/clearOverrides in the hook
- migrate effectiveAnalysis and handleGenerate
- replace the 8 prop pairs on AnalysisResults with 2
- run the a11y, contrast, stale, unreadable and precision suites

## Expected impact
Developers: one reset site, fewer props; users: no override can survive an image swap. Could break: the adjustments payload shape if keys drift - pin it in a test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one override state, one reset
Before: 4 override states, 8 hand-listed reset calls in 2 sites, 16 AnalysisResults props
After: predicted 1 state, 1 reset call, 10 props
Method: simulation - counted on the tree; the M refactor across 3 files with risk 4 is a Lane B worktree job
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: useMaterialStyleTransfer.ts: setOverrideRoughness(null)/setOverrideMetallic(null)/setOverrideEmissive(null)/setOverrideSurface(null) in acceptFile and handleClearImage; AnalysisResults.tsx AnalysisResultsProps: 16 fields
instrument: count of override useState + reset call sites + AnalysisResults props before/after, with every MaterialStyleTransfer suite green

title: Decide what Analyze does with an image and no description while the analyzer cannot see images
body:
## Summary
Analyze is enabled with only an image attached, but the analyzer reads text only, so an image-only run always returns the default stone material.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/materials/MaterialStyleTransfer/index.tsx Analyze button: `disabled={isAnalyzing || (!imageDataUrl && !referenceDescription.trim())}` - an image alone enables it. src/app/api/style-transfer/route.ts:17 ignores the bytes (imageAnalyzed: false) and with an empty description returns stone / grey palette / 0.4 confidence. The route names wiring @/lib/vision a deliberate non-goal because it would put a metered call behind the button. Two honest options: (a) require a description until a vision seam is opted into, or (b) wire @/lib/vision behind an explicit opt-in. Either changes what the feature IS - an owner call.

## Flow
- user drops a screenshot, leaves the description empty, clicks Analyze
- route returns the stone default
- panel shows a full analysis that came from no input

## Expected impact
Users stop receiving a fabricated-looking analysis from no input; (b) adds cost. Could break: e2e that analyze with an image only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an analysis only runs on an input the analyzer reads
Before: image-only Analyze enabled; 1 of 1 image-only runs returns the hardcoded default
After: (a) 0 image-only runs; (b) image-informed values at a metered cost
Method: simulation - the choice between (a) and (b) is a product/cost decision, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/app/api/style-transfer/route.ts:16-20 hasImage = !!body.imageDataUrl; analyzeFromDescription(description, hasImage) -> imageAnalyzed: false
src/app/api/style-transfer/route.ts:42-49 vision seam a deliberate non-goal (metered)
instrument: owner decision (a) gate on description vs (b) opt-in @/lib/vision
